page.text:
# LAURA
MELAHN
for Menlo Park City Council · District 4
Housing solutionsDowntown leadershipFiscal responsibility
Love Menlo. Vote Laura.
DonateJoin 10/18 Giving Day
A letter from Laura
My name is Laura Melahn, and I am running to represent District 4 on Menlo Park’s City Council.
I’m running because I love this place. I believe the good life is building something meaningful with other people in the place you share. But the way Menlo Park City Council is operating today is pushing residents out of civic engagement. I want to help make decisions that make sense to the people who have to live with them.
My friends and neighbors saw my candidacy coming a mile away: when I galvanized our neighborhood to help make our streets safer for kids walking and biking, and built a citywide plan in the process; when I pulled our street together to save a 90-year-old heritage tree from developer destruction; and when I started a nonprofit dedicated to the simple goal of making our Downtown more inviting.
I don’t want to be a City Councilmember in the abstract. I want to help Menlo Park do right by our residents, our businesses, and the physical place we are all so lucky to call home.
Over the past several years, I’ve watched our City Council listen to everyone except the people who live here. That is what I will do differently.
I’m running for the people of Menlo Park. I’m obviously not a career politician. If I were, I’d have better hair and smoother speeches. But I do know what it feels like to have my neighborhood’s concerns dismissed by our district representative. It’s terrible. So let’s change that.
Love Menlo? Me too.
Laura Melahn
Laura at a Glance
Co-founder, 501(c)(3) nonprofit Downtown Menlo Fund
Chair, Menlo Park Finance & Audit Commission
Creator, downtownmenlo.com & lovemenlo.com
Author, Ollie’s First Day: An Oak Knoll Story
Volunteer Coach, Menlo Park AYSO & Alpine Little League
Board Member, The MAVEN Project
Co-founder, Meadow Valley Partners
Princeton University, Molecular Biology
The Slow Streets Lady
You might have some questions.
## Let’s answer them.
Do you know how to do this job?
Yes, I do, because I weirdly love it. I also like long distance running and once did a wall sit for 30 minutes, so there are some throughlines. There’s a short list of people who have attended more City Council meetings than I have these past few years and I’d wager no one who has watched more historical City Council YouTube content or read more agenda packets. The reason is, I believe in first-principles thinking, a prepared mind, and primary sources, so I’ve spent the time understanding how and why historical decisions have been made and what’s at stake for the future.
I’m the Chair of Menlo Park’s Finance and Audit Commission and the Managing Partner of an investment firm, which turns out to be relevant for the coming years in Menlo Park, as we face a structural budget deficit that will require attention and fiscal responsibility.
Who are you, “Laura Melahn”?
Quick hits: I was born and raised in Hawaii, where I played endless amounts of soccer; studied molecular biology at Princeton, where I ran countless laps around the track; then did biochemistry research at Oxford University, where I again played lots of soccer. I arrived in the Bay Area 19 years ago and built a career at Google and GV, then put down roots with my husband and two boys in Menlo Park 6 years ago. In the community I coach soccer and baseball, convene weekly neighbor nights, wrote two books with Oak Knoll educators, and sit on the boards of both a healthcare access and downtown revitalization nonprofit. Professionally I’m a co-founder of Meadow Valley Partners, a healthcare investment fund and the CEO of Mauka Bio.
What would you care about as a Menlo Park councilmember?
I care about people, place, and process. People means listening to residents and valuing their quality of life. Place means protecting our city’s parks, heritage trees, open spaces, Downtown, and neighborhoods. Process means fiscal responsibility, logical decision making, effective execution, and accurate data.
Our City government has a mission: “It is the mission of the City government to ensure that Menlo Park is a desirable and vibrant community in which to live and do business, and to respond to the values and priorities of the residents so as to provide for the community’s current and future needs.” It’s my goal to help the City live up to that stated mission.
Read the full plan →
Have you accomplished anything useful for the people of Menlo Park?
- I serve as the Chair of the Menlo Park Finance and Audit Commission, bringing analytical rigor to our fiscal commission.
- I co-founded the 501(c)(3) nonprofit Downtown Menlo Fund to support local businesses and bring investment downtown. This summer we launched Fourth Fridays bringing live music and good times to Santa Cruz Ave every month.
- I created downtownmenlo.com and the brand Love Menlo to drive placemaking and visibility for Downtown Menlo Park.
- I advocated for modernizing what types of businesses are allowed on Santa Cruz Ave through the Planning Commission process. Allowing more community-serving businesses is good for residents and for the vibrancy of Downtown. In particular, small-scale commercial recreation was not in staff’s draft plan. We advocated for it, got it in, and it’s why a family activity center can now open downtown!
- Making our neighborhood streets safer for kids, walkers, bikers, pets, and all was my entry point to engagement with the City. I’ve advocated for re-starting the paused Slow Streets Program to make our City more conducive to community building, social health, and safety. I’ve consistently encouraged that we try faster and less expensive pilots that are validated by other municipalities. A new Slow Streets Program was adopted in April 2026.
- I partnered with Oak Knoll educators to write Ollie’s First Day and Ollie Gets Ready, helping children who spent their earliest years in the pandemic make the transition to kindergarten. Custom versions of the book for Encinal and Laurel will launch this fall.
What about housing in the downtown parking lots?
It’s the question that has consumed this city for three years while producing zero building permits. It’s also worth being precise about the problem. Menlo Park is ahead of pace on market-rate homes, 59% of our target with five years to go, because the market builds those on its own. What we’re short of is very-low-income homes, the kind a preschool teacher or a home health aide can afford. That’s the dial to move, and it’s exactly the dial my plan moves.
My housing plan works whether November’s initiative passes or fails, because most of Menlo Park’s affordable housing opportunity isn’t on the parking lots at all. It’s at Parkline, one block from downtown, and at the USGS campus, and it’s negotiable right now, before the election. It’s even on Marsh Road, where the David D. Bohannon Organization has spent years asking the city for permission to build housing on its own land.
Any downtown project gets the same test from me as everything else: does it pencil, and does it deliver very-low-income homes. As submitted, every one of the three current proposals gives something up: the very-low-income homes, the no-cost parking, or real construction wages. If we put everything from maintenance to economic development on hold behind one development idea, we’ll find ourselves trying to resuscitate Downtown as a dead patient. The best is yet to come for Downtown Menlo Park, and my plan doesn’t make anyone wait for it.
Read the housing plan →
Are you against housing downtown?
No. Housing downtown is a good thing, and my plan shows it: Parkline will put hundreds of homes one block from downtown and equidistant to the train station. Any project on the plazas themselves gets the same test from me as every other site, does it pencil and does it deliver. What I’m against is confusing good intentions with a plan. The current plan promised 345 or more affordable homes by 2027; it’s 2026 and there are zero permits. When someone says healthcare is broken, nobody thinks they’re anti-healthcare. Saying this plan is broken doesn’t make me anti-housing. It makes me the candidate who published a better one: the housing plan.
## Ask the people I’ve worked with
Every endorsement here comes from someone who knows me and my work, from Menlo Park neighbors to former mayors to a former Governor and Secretary of the Navy.
Endorsed by city leaders
Ray Mueller
San Mateo County Supervisor & Former Mayor of Menlo Park
John Boyle
Former Vice Mayor of Menlo Park
Catherine Carlton
Former Mayor of Menlo Park
Paul Collacchi
Former Mayor of Menlo Park
Peter Ohtaki
Former Mayor of Menlo Park
Steve Schmidt
Former Mayor of Menlo Park
Virginia Chang Kiraly
President, Menlo Park Fire Protection District Board
Rob Silano
Menlo Park Fire Protection District Board Vice President
“
I owe my career to California’s public schools, so I take seriously what a city does with the public’s money. A city is an economic system: a decision about one block of downtown affects the tax base and what the City can afford to do for everyone else. Laura Melahn understands that. She asks what a decision will actually do before she decides whether she is for it, which is rarer than it should be, and I am supporting her for City Council.
Robert Hall Nobel Laureate in Economics, 2026; Professor of Economics, Stanford
“
I only endorse people I actually know. I've worked with Laura and seen firsthand what she's capable of: she outworks everyone and she delivers results. Menlo Park would be fortunate to have her fighting for its future.
Ray Mabus 75th United States Secretary of the Navy
“
The choice is easy. Laura’s candidacy comes at a perfect time. The city needs a council member who can rise above divisiveness and find workable alternatives. Laura’s downtown revitalization project tells us how city problems can and should be solved. Clear thinking, enthusiasm and working together is Laura’s magic.
Steve Schmidt Former Mayor of Menlo Park
“
At HUD I saw a great many housing programs announced with confidence and never financed, usually because the promise came first and the economics came later, if at all. Laura Melahn starts by asking how a project will be paid for and whether the homes will actually get built. Menlo Park needs more affordable housing, and in my experience that is what it takes to get it built. I am supporting Laura for City Council.
Susan Woodward Former Chief Economist, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development; Former Chief Economist, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
“
Laura is uniquely qualified to manage the complex financial negotiations demanded by the constant stream of large scale development projects facing Menlo Park. Menlo Park has needed someone this bright with these skills for a very long time. Put her to work on the city council as fast as you can.
Paul Collacchi Former Mayor of Menlo Park
“
Laura was an amazing help as I prepared to open OFFLINE Pilates in Menlo Park. I knew the city from having worked here, but I had never navigated it as a business owner, and finding the right space was proving harder than I expected. Laura told me about the changes happening downtown and how they could benefit a business like mine. We grabbed coffee, talked about the city, and walked the streets together as she showed me available storefronts. She told me what she wants to do to make Menlo Park even better, and she connected me with city officials who were wonderful to work with. That’s the kind of person Menlo Park needs on City Council! Makini Mask Founder, OFFLINE Pilates
Makini Mask OFFLINE Pilates
“
Clear headed and intelligent. Laura understands the needs of the Downtown business community. Most important, she is grounded in fiscal responsibility and the necessary management metrics for creating government efficiencies. Draeger's Markets strongly endorses her candidacy.
Richard Draeger Draeger's Super Markets, Inc.
“
Family and kid focus. Smart as a whip. Loves Menlo and will help transform the City for the future.
Ben Eiref Former Planning Commission Chair
“
Laura is the kind of neighbor who gets things done for Menlo Park. She partners with our teachers, builds for our community, and shows up when it counts. She’s who we need on Council.
Jennifer Baskin Former Parks and Recreation Commission Chair
